(Currently Amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, and wherein said directional control valve is configured to selectively allow air to flow from the booster device to the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, and wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, and wherein said path is configured to allow for the flow of air to be filtered before reaching the pump.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 4, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, wherein the filter is positioned to prevent contaminants from entering the pump.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, and wherein the method further includes monitoring the operational status of the braking system.

(Currently Amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, and wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to allow air to flow from the booster device to the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, and wherein the directional control valve is configured to selectively allow air to flow from the booster device to the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, and wherein the system is configured to monitor the pressure differential across the pump.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, and wherein the system includes a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, wherein the filter is positioned to prevent contaminants from entering the pump.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, and wherein the system is configured to monitor the operational status of the braking system.

(Currently Amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced, and wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to allow air to flow from the booster device to the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, and wherein the directional control valve is configured to selectively allow air to flow from the booster device to the atmosphere.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, and wherein the system is configured to monitor the pressure differential across the pump.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, and wherein the vehicle includes a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system, and wherein the system is configured to monitor the operational status of the braking system.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type, and wherein the vehicle is configured to optimize performance based on engine load conditions.
